title: Let there be light
told: the first page of the Bible

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? ever stared at a blank page and not known where to start?
options: then this one was written for you. listen to how the bible starts.
hold onto that. the very first page starts exactly there.
good. keep this one for the next new beginning.

steps.line: Before anything existed, the earth was formless and empty, and darkness was on the face of the deep.

steps.q: Everything is dark. God makes light first. What does God do with the darkness?
o: Separates it, and names it Night
steps.why: Genesis 1:4-5: God separates light from darkness and names them Day and Night. The dark isn’t destroyed; it gets a place and a name.

steps.line: Then God said, “Let there be light.” And there was light.
steps.label: Genesis 1:3

steps.line: Day by day, the world was made. The sky opened above the sea.
steps.label: Genesis 1

steps.q: The Hebrew word for the sky on day two, raqia, pictures something specific. What?
o: A dome stretched over the waters
steps.why: Raqia comes from a verb for hammering metal thin. Ancient listeners pictured a great dome holding back the waters above.

steps.line: Land and trees. The sun, the moon and the stars.
steps.label: Genesis 1

steps.q: Here’s a puzzle readers love: light comes on day one, but the sun isn’t made until day four. What might that be saying?
o: The writers mixed up the order
The sun was there, just hidden
The first light came from God’s word
steps.why: Many readers notice this. The first light comes straight from a word. Genesis doesn’t even name the sun, just “the greater light,” as if to say it’s no god.

steps.line: Fish in the water, birds in the air, and animals of every kind.
steps.label: Genesis 1

steps.line: And finally, people. Again and again, the same words: “God saw that it was good.” The Bible’s first story is a story about starting.
steps.label: Genesis 1:31

steps.q: In the ancient world, a king might be called the image of a god. Genesis 1 says who is made in God’s image?
steps.why: Genesis 1:27: “in the image of God he created them; male and female.” A title kept for kings is handed to everyone.

say: here’s what i love. the bible’s very first story isn’t a rule. it’s a beginning.
christians read it as a promise: God makes something good out of nothing. a blank page isn’t empty. it’s where creation starts.

steps.q: Genesis goes on: on the seventh day, God stops and rests. Why would a story about making the world end with rest?
o: God was tired after six days
Nothing else was left to make
Rest is part of the making
steps.why: Jewish and Christian readers see the seventh day as holy: the Sabbath. Rest is built into creation itself.

today.say: pick one thing you’ve been putting off. do the first five minutes of it today, before you feel ready.
options: that’s how every beginning goes. in the dark, one word first.
Something came to mind, not today
that counts. you’ve already named it. that’s the first word.

tomorrow.title: Abram packs up.
tomorrow.line: he’s seventy-five, he has no map, and he goes anyway.
